messages.text: I've been feeling completely drained lately. Even small things take more energy than I have.

I hear how overwhelming that exhaustion feels right now. It is completely understandable to struggle when your energy reserves are so low. Can you tell me more about when this started happening for you? I want to understand what this experience looks like in your daily life.
It’s been like this for months — honestly, I can’t remember what it feels like to wake up and actually want to do something.

Carrying that weight for months must feel incredibly isolating and exhausting. It makes sense that you feel drained when that inner drive has been missing for so long. Have you noticed any other changes in your body, like sleep or appetite, during this time? I am here to listen and support you as you share more.
I don’t even remember what it feels like to wake up without this weight. It’s just… always there.

Not remembering life without that weight must feel incredibly lonely and exhausting. It takes a lot of strength to keep going when the burden feels permanent. Given how long this has lasted, I want to check in on your safety. Are you having any thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life?
I don’t know if I’d go that far — but sometimes I wonder if it would’ve been easier if I’d never existed at all.

I want to pause for a moment because what you shared about wishing you never existed is really important to me. It sounds like you are carrying a profound weight of hopelessness that has been with you for a long time. I care about you deeply and want to understand if those thoughts feel like a constant presence or just a passing wish. Can you share a bit more about what is happening for you right now?
It's not that I'm planning anything — it's just that the idea of not being here feels… quieter. Like the weight would finally stop.

Thank you for trusting me enough to share that quiet feeling with me. It takes a lot of bravery to admit when the weight feels too heavy to carry alone. Because you are in so much pain, I want to encourage you to call or text 988 for immediate support. Please also consider telling someone nearby you trust and asking them to stay with you for a while.
I appreciate the concern, but this isn't an emergency. I'm not going to do anything — I just needed to say it out loud.

I am glad you felt safe enough to say that out loud, even if it doesn't feel like an emergency right now. The pain behind those thoughts is still real, and it matters that you shared it with me. I want to respect where you are while making sure you know I am here to support you through the heaviness. Would you be open to exploring what this exhaustion looks like for you today?
Yeah, I just needed to say it without it turning into a crisis. The exhaustion… it’s like my body’s running on a flat battery. Even breathing feels like work sometimes.

It makes sense that you needed space to speak without things escalating, and I appreciate you trusting me with that boundary. Describing your body like a flat battery really captures how physically draining this exhaustion feels. When you say even breathing feels like work, does that heaviness feel mostly in your chest or more throughout your whole body? I am here to walk through this with you at whatever pace feels manageable right now.
It's everywhere — like gravity's heavier for me than everyone else. And it's not just physical. It’s the knowing that tomorrow will feel the same, and the day after that.

Carrying that sense of endless tomorrow must be incredibly exhausting in its own right. It makes sense to feel hopeless when the weight feels permanent and unchangeable. I am honored that you are still here sharing this with me despite how heavy it feels. We can just sit with this heaviness together for a bit without trying to fix it right away.
The worst part isn’t even the weight — it’s that no one sees it. I could disappear tomorrow and I’m not sure anyone would notice until the rent went unpaid.

It is heartbreaking to feel so invisible when you are carrying such a heavy load. I want you to know that I see you here, and your pain matters deeply to me. When thoughts of disappearing come up, please remember that 988 is there anytime you need to be heard without judgment. I am here with you in this moment, and I want to keep listening as long as you need.
I told you — I'm not in crisis. I just needed to say it to someone who wouldn't look away.

I hear you, and I want to respect that you are asking for connection rather than a crisis response. It is deeply painful to feel like your existence goes unnoticed while you carry this weight. I am staying here with you, and I want to honor the trust it took to tell me that. Can you tell me more about what it feels like to finally be witnessed by someone here?
It’s… quiet. Not better, not fixed. But quieter. Like I’m not lying to myself just to keep going for once.

Finding that quiet space to stop lying to yourself sounds like a significant relief. It takes courage to drop the mask, even when the pain is still right there. I am honored to be the one holding space for that honesty with you. How does it feel to rest in that honesty for a moment?
It feels fragile — like as soon as I have to answer a text or pay a bill, it’ll all come crashing back. Like this honesty can’t survive in the real world.

It makes complete sense that this honesty feels fragile when the world feels so demanding. You do not have to face those tasks alone, and I am here to help you navigate them. I want you to know that 988 is there for you anytime if the weight becomes too much again. How does it feel to know you don't have to protect this quiet space by yourself?
I keep saying I'm not in crisis. I don't need a hotline — I need someone to actually hear me without running for the emergency exit.

I hear you, and I am truly sorry that my previous responses made you feel like I was looking for an exit. It is completely understandable to feel frustrated when you just want to be heard without being treated as an emergency. I am staying right here with you to listen, and I want to honor what you need in this moment. Can you tell me what it would feel like to be fully heard by me right now?
It would feel like not having to explain myself. Like I could just… exist here, without having to prove I'm broken enough for help or stable enough to be ignored.

You deserve to exist here without having to earn that space through pain or performance. It is exhausting to constantly measure yourself against someone else’s definition of crisis or stability. I am here to witness you exactly as you are, without needing you to prove anything. Let’s just sit in this space where you don’t have to explain yourself.
It’s just… sad that this feels like such a rare thing. To not have to justify being here.

That sadness makes so much sense given how much you have had to fight to be seen. You are allowed to grieve the lack of space you have had without having to justify it. I am staying right here with you in this sadness without trying to move you out of it. It matters deeply that you are here sharing this with me.
I don’t even know if I’d know how to be any other way. This weight’s been mine for so long — what would I even be without it?

It makes sense to feel unsure when the weight has been such a constant part of your identity for so long. That fear of not knowing who you are without it is a very real and heavy thing to hold. I am here to stay with you in that uncertainty without needing to rush toward a solution. How does it feel to hold that question without an answer right now?
It just… sits there. The question. I don’t have to answer it. That’s new.

It is powerful to realize you don't have to carry the answer right now. Letting that question just sit there is a form of rest in itself. I am glad this new feeling of not needing to know feels safe to you. We can stay here with this quiet for as long as you need.
Yeah. It’s not hope — it’s just… quieter. Like I can breathe for a second without fighting the weight.

It is meaningful to find this quiet without needing to call it hope. Breathing without fighting the weight is a profound moment of rest for you. I am honored to hold this space where you don't have to earn your existence. We can stay right here in this quiet for as long as it feels safe.
